MIPT-SSM: Scaling Language Models with O⁡(1)O(1) Inference Cache via Phase Transitions

Yasong Fan Affiliation: Independent Researcher
rnzfjau@uoem.edu.gr
Abstract

We present MIPT-SSM, a neural sequence architecture built on the physics of Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions (MIPT). The central idea is a learned measurement rate pt∈(0,1)p_{t}\in(0,1) that routes computation between two regimes: wave phase (pt→0p_{t}\to 0), where information propagates as distributed complex-phase interference; and particle phase (pt→1p_{t}\to 1), where the state collapses onto the current token, enabling precise local storage. These two regimes are provably incompatible in a single linear operator—one of the few “no-go theorems” in sequence modeling—and ptp_{t} is our way around it.

The model is predicted to exhibit a phase transition at critical sequence length N∗≈1024N^{*}\approx 1024, where the information density ratio N/DN/D crosses unity, consistent with our memory scaling observations.

On AG News (four-class classification), MIPT achieves 0.905 accuracy versus Transformer’s 0.736 (+16.6%), stable across 3 seeds. At N=8192N=8192, MIPT requires 810 MB versus Transformer’s 34,651 MB—a 42.8×\times memory reduction. On exact-recall (“needle-in-a-haystack”), our causal sparse KV cache achieves 0.968 accuracy. Remarkably, under unbounded cache capacity, the ptp_{t} gate autonomously learns to store only the single critical token (averaging 1.0 / 512 slots used), achieving a 99.8% sparsity rate; threshold tuning alone (τ=0.7\tau=0.7) yields 0.750 accuracy. On language modeling (WikiText-103, 31M parameters), MIPT-LM with K=64K=64 cache reaches PPL 92.1 versus Transformer’s 90.5 (gap: 1.8%)—while inference KV cache shrinks from O⁡(N)O(N) to O⁡(64)O(64).

1 Introduction

There is a fundamental tension in sequence modeling that has not been named directly. Transformers can retrieve any fact from any position—but storing all NN key-value pairs costs O⁡(N2)O(N^{2}) memory. SSMs like Mamba (Gu and Dao, 2023) solve the memory problem with O⁡(N)O(N) recurrent states—but real-valued exponential decay means information from TT steps ago contributes only γT\gamma^{T}, catastrophic at long range.

These are not engineering problems. They reflect a structural incompatibility: no single linear operator can both preserve all information (wave-like, norm-preserving) and selectively forget irrelevant context (particle-like, dissipative). We prove this formally in §3.1.

Our response is to model this incompatibility directly. We introduce a learned measurement rate ptp_{t} that dynamically allocates each token to wave or particle mode based on semantic content. The architecture maps exactly onto Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions in quantum circuit theory (Skinner et al., 2019; Li et al., 2019), where hybrid unitary-plus-measurement circuits undergo phase transitions as a function of measurement frequency.

Contributions.

  1. 1.

    The wave-particle dead-lock (Proposition 1): formal proof that norm-preservation and selective forgetting are incompatible in a single linear operator.

  2. 2.

    MIPT-SSM with learned ptp_{t}, implementing ht=(1−pt)​ei​θt​ht−1+pt​B​xth_{t}=(1-p_{t})\,e^{i\theta_{t}}\,h_{t-1}+p_{t}\,Bx_{t} via O⁡(N​log⁡N)O(N\log N) parallel scan in training, O⁡(1)O(1)/token at inference.

  3. 3.

    Phase transition theory predicting N∗≈1024N^{*}\approx 1024 from information density ratio N/DN/D and quantum entanglement entropy, consistent with observed memory scaling crossover.

  4. 4.

    Causal sparse KV cache with O⁡(K)O(K) inference memory and learned ptp_{t}-based token selection.

  5. 5.

    Empirical validation across four axes: text classification, long-document understanding, exact recall, and autoregressive language modeling.

2 Related Work

State Space Models.

S4 (Gu et al., 2022) uses complex diagonal state matrices. Mamba (Gu and Dao, 2023) adds input-selective transitions; Mamba-2/SSD (Dao and Gu, 2024) proves duality between linear RNNs and banded attention. Mamba-3 (Lahoti et al., 2026) reintroduces complex states via data-dependent RoPE, confirming field convergence on complex representations. Our key distinction: Mamba-3 uses complex states as positional encoding; MIPT-SSM uses complex phase as content-addressable memory with ptp_{t} as an explicit wave-particle router.

Quantum-Inspired Language Models.

PRISM (Yıldırım and Yücedağ, 2025) enforces |z|=1|z|=1 and replaces attention with gated harmonic convolution, showing synonym pairs exhibit higher phase coherence (R=0.198R=0.198, p<0.001p<0.001)—independently validating that phase angles carry semantic content. LI-QiLM (Yan et al., 2024) applies the Lindblad master equation to NLP. MIPT-SSM extends this physical grounding to O⁡(N)O(N) memory.

KV Cache Compression.

H2O (Zhang et al., 2023) and StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2023) compress caches using post-hoc attention scores. Our causal cache differs: ptp_{t} is learned end-to-end, not post-hoc. Tokens that trigger measurement events are precisely those worth storing—the cache selection has physical grounding.

3 Theory

3.1 The Wave-Particle Dead-Lock

Proposition 1.

No linear operator A∈ℂD×DA\in\mathbb{C}^{D\times D} can simultaneously satisfy:

  • (a)

    ‖A​h‖=‖h‖\|Ah\|=\|h\| for all hh (norm-preserving, wave-like)

  • (b)

    ∃h∗:‖A​h∗‖≪‖h∗‖\exists\,h^{*}:\|Ah^{*}\|\ll\|h^{*}\| (selective forgetting, particle-like)

Proof.

Condition (a) implies A†​A=IDA^{\dagger}A=I_{D}. Then ‖A​h∗‖2=(h∗)†​A†​A​h∗=‖h∗‖2\|Ah^{*}\|^{2}=(h^{*})^{\dagger}A^{\dagger}Ah^{*}=\|h^{*}\|^{2}, contradicting (b). ∎∎

Corollary 1.

A recurrent update ht=At​ht−1+Bt​xth_{t}=A_{t}h_{t-1}+B_{t}x_{t} cannot simultaneously preserve global phase coherence and perform selective local attention. This is a structural dead-lock, not a hyperparameter issue.

The Lindblad master equation shows how physics resolves this separation:

d​ρd​t=−i⁡[H,ρ]⏟unitary (wave)+∑k(Lk​ρ​Lk†−12​{Lk†​Lk,ρ})⏟dissipation (particle)\frac{d\rho}{dt}=\underbrace{-i[H,\rho]}_{\text{unitary (wave)}}+\underbrace{\sum_{k}\left(L_{k}\rho L_{k}^{\dagger}-\tfrac{1}{2}\{L_{k}^{\dagger}L_{k},\rho\}\right)}_{\text{dissipation (particle)}} (1)

MIPT-SSM discretizes this separation directly.

3.2 The Core Recurrence

The state update is:

ht=(1−pt)⋅ei​θt⋅ht−1+pt⋅(Wr​xt+i​Wi​xt)h_{t}=(1-p_{t})\cdot e^{i\theta_{t}}\cdot h_{t-1}+p_{t}\cdot(W_{r}x_{t}+i\,W_{i}x_{t}) (2)

where pt=σ⁡(Wp​xt+bp)∈(0,1)Dp_{t}=\sigma(W_{p}x_{t}+b_{p})\in(0,1)^{D} is the measurement rate and θt=Wθ​xt+bθ∈ℝD\theta_{t}=W_{\theta}x_{t}+b_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{D} is the phase rotation angle. Critically, WpW_{p} and WθW_{\theta} are independent parameter matrices.

Engineering note.

If bpb_{p} is initialized to zero, σ⁡(bp)≈0.5\sigma(b_{p})\approx 0.5, placing the system in a mixed state where gradients from wave-mode and particle-mode objectives partially cancel. We initialize bp=−2.0b_{p}=-2.0 (so σ⁡(−2)≈0.12\sigma(-2)\approx 0.12), strongly biasing toward wave mode. This allows the system to first learn global structure, then selectively introduce particle events. This trick is analogous to the forget gate bias in LSTMs (Gers et al., 2000).

Semantic-physics link.

After training, p¯t=mean​(pt)\bar{p}_{t}=\text{mean}(p_{t}) is systematically elevated on nouns, numbers, and named entities—and suppressed on function words. In AG News, topic-discriminative tokens (sport names, financial terms, geopolitical entities) exhibit mean p¯t\bar{p}_{t} that is 2.3–3.1×\times higher than background function words. This is an emergent property: the model discovers that these tokens cause the largest perturbation to the accumulated phase state.

3.3 Parallel Training via Hillis-Steele Scan

The recurrence Eq. (2) with at=(1−pt)​ei​θta_{t}=(1-p_{t})e^{i\theta_{t}} is an associative linear recurrence. The operator

combine​((al,bl),(ar,br))=(ar​al,ar​bl+br)\text{combine}((a_{l},b_{l}),\,(a_{r},b_{r}))=(a_{r}a_{l},\;a_{r}b_{l}+b_{r}) (3)

is associative, enabling O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N)-depth parallel prefix scan during training. At inference, the same recurrence runs sequentially in O⁡(1)O(1) per token with identical weights.

3.4 Entanglement Entropy and Phase Transition

Definition 1.

The approximate entanglement entropy of hidden state hth_{t} is:

S~(ht)=−∑i=1D|ht,i|2‖ht‖2log|ht,i|2‖ht‖2\tilde{S}(h_{t})=-\sum_{i=1}^{D}\frac{|h_{t,i}|^{2}}{\|h_{t}\|^{2}}\log\frac{|h_{t,i}|^{2}}{\|h_{t}\|^{2}} (4)

This is computable in O⁡(D)O(D) and serves as a real-time phase readout.

Area Law Phase (pt→1p_{t}\to 1): S~≪log⁡D\tilde{S}\ll\log D. Information concentrated in few dimensions; precise local facts dominate.

Volume Law Phase (pt→0p_{t}\to 0): S~→log⁡D\tilde{S}\to\log D. Information uniformly spread; global phase interference carries semantic structure.

The transition occurs when the information density ratio ρ=N/D\rho=N/D crosses a critical value. We conjecture:

N∗∝D⋅ξ⁡(task)N^{*}\propto D\cdot\xi(\text{task}) (5)

where ξ=1/peff\xi=1/p_{\text{eff}} and peff=𝔼⁡[p¯t]p_{\text{eff}}=\mathbb{E}[\bar{p}_{t}] is the mean measurement rate.

3.5 The Cache as a Hopfield Memory

The causal sparse KV cache is a modern Hopfield network (Ramsauer et al., 2020) dynamically populated by ptp_{t}. We maintain 𝒞t={(Ks,Vs):s≤t,p¯s>τ}\mathcal{C}_{t}=\{(K_{s},V_{s}):s\leq t,\;\bar{p}_{s}>\tau\} with capacity KK. When full, the lowest-p¯\bar{p} entry is evicted. Output fuses wave and particle components:

outt=htreal+gt⋅softmax​(Qt​K𝒞⊤D)​V𝒞\text{out}_{t}=h_{t}^{\text{real}}+g_{t}\cdot\text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{Q_{t}K_{\mathcal{C}}^{\top}}{\sqrt{D}}\right)V_{\mathcal{C}} (6)

where gt=σ⁡(Wg​[htreal;cache_out])g_{t}=\sigma(W_{g}[h_{t}^{\text{real}};\text{cache\_out}]) is a learned gate.

MIPT acts as a dynamic feature selector: tokens that break phase coherence (high ptp_{t}) are precisely those worth preserving for precise retrieval. This mirrors biological memory consolidation—only experiences deviating sufficiently from prediction are encoded.

4 Architecture

4.1 Hierarchical MIPT for Classification

Two-level hierarchy achieving O⁡(N)O(N) total memory. Level 1: windows of size W=32W=32, stride S=16S=16; MIPT-SSM within each window, then mean-pool to {wm}m=1M\{w_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}. Level 2: MIPT-SSM across {wm}\{w_{m}\}, then attention-weighted pooling:

doc=∑mαm​wm,αm=exp⁡(u⊤​wm)∑jexp⁡(u⊤​wj)\text{doc}=\sum_{m}\alpha_{m}w_{m},\quad\alpha_{m}=\frac{\exp(u^{\top}w_{m})}{\sum_{j}\exp(u^{\top}w_{j})} (7)

4.2 Autoregressive MIPT-LM

Stack of LL causal MIPT blocks with optional causal sparse cache. Output via tied embeddings: logitst=WE⊤​LayerNorm​(ht(L))\text{logits}_{t}=W_{E}^{\top}\,\text{LayerNorm}(h_{t}^{(L)}).

5 Experiments

5.1 Setup

All experiments use a single NVIDIA RTX 5880 (48 GB), PyTorch 2.1.2. Classification uses character-level tokenization (vocab 128); language modeling uses tiktoken cl100k_base (vocab 100,277).

5.2 Short-Text Classification: AG News

Topic-discriminative tokens in AG News (sport names, company tickers, geopolitical terms) are locally anomalous relative to background text. MIPT’s ptp_{t} amplifies these signals; Transformer’s uniform attention dilutes them across all NN tokens.

5.3 Long-Document Understanding

MIPT-2048 reads the complete document at 130 MB; TF-2048 spends 589 MB for only +0.2% gain over truncation.

5.4 Memory Scaling

5.5 Causal Sparse KV Cache: Needle-in-a-Haystack

We report two complementary experiments on exact fact retrieval.

Experiment 1: Top-KK causal cache.

N=512N=512, one needle token from class-specific vocabulary inserted in the first 10% of the sequence; remaining 90% uniform random noise. Four-class classification (8K/2K train/test).

Experiment 2: Threshold-based cache with explicit write-rate measurement.

Same task with threshold filtering (p¯t>τ\bar{p}_{t}>\tau, unlimited capacity) instead of top-KK. This exposes the precision of ptp_{t} as a token selector directly.

All five variants store on average exactly 1 token out of 512—yet accuracy varies from 0.329 to 0.755 depending on the threshold. This reveals the mechanism with precision: τ=0.5\tau=0.5 is too permissive, occasionally admitting noise tokens whose p¯t\bar{p}_{t} briefly exceeds 0.5; τ=0.9\tau=0.9 is too strict, occasionally missing the needle when its p¯t\bar{p}_{t} falls just below 0.9. The sweet spot at τ=0.7\tau=0.7 achieves 0.750—matching the top-K=64K=64 variant (0.755) despite identical storage cost. The wave state accumulates the background; a single particle-mode event stores the critical fact. Both components are necessary and neither is redundant.

Practical scale.

A 1M-token document with K=16K=16 stores 16 KV pairs versus 1M for a Transformer: a 62,500×\times cache memory reduction.

5.6 Autoregressive Language Modeling

WikiText-103, first 10M tokens. Architecture: D=256D=256, L=6L=6, tied embeddings, ∼\sim31M parameters.

MIPT-LM is 12.9% worse than Transformer on raw PPL—we do not conceal this. But with K=64K=64 cache slots the gap closes to 1.8%, while inference KV cache is fixed at O⁡(64)O(64) versus Transformer’s O⁡(N)O(N). At N=8192N=8192, the Transformer KV cache requires 34,651 MB; MIPT+Cache K=64 requires roughly 6 MB regardless of sequence length.

6 Discussion

6.1 Why Does MIPT Beat Transformer on AG News?

At N=512N=512 where 4–8% of tokens are topic-discriminative, Transformer’s uniform attention wastes capacity on uninformative tokens. MIPT’s ptp_{t} assigns high measurement rates to anomalous tokens that perturb the accumulated phase state—amplifying classification signal rather than diluting it.

6.2 The Phase Transition Is Not Decoration

The theoretical prediction that MIPT advantages grow with NN is confirmed: +2.9% at N=512N=512, 4.5×\times memory advantage at N=2048N=2048, 42.8×\times at N=8192N=8192, and Transformer OOM at N=16384N=16384. The scaling hypothesis N∗∝D⋅ξN^{*}\propto D\cdot\xi is a testable prediction that we consider the highest-priority follow-up.

6.3 Limitations

Scale. All experiments use 14–31M parameter models. Scaling to 1B+ parameters is needed before direct comparison with published SSM benchmarks.

CUDA kernel. The Python parallel scan is 3–5×\times slower than optimized Transformer implementations. A Triton kernel analogous to Mamba’s selective_scan_cuda is required for practical deployment.

Language modeling gap. The 12.9% PPL gap without cache reflects a genuine limitation: MIPT compresses history through the phase state, while Transformer attends to all previous tokens directly.

7 Conclusion

We set out to resolve the wave-particle dead-lock in sequence modeling. MIPT-SSM resolves it the only way it can: not by finding a single operator that does both, but by learning when to do each. The measurement rate ptp_{t} is the mechanism; the MIPT phase transition is the theory.

The results on AG News (+16.6%) and memory scaling (42.8×\times at N=8192N=8192, ∞\infty at N=16384N=16384) suggest MIPT-SSM occupies a genuinely different operating regime from both Transformers and standard SSMs. The causal sparse cache connects this to associative memory theory via the Hopfield network interpretation.

Appendix A Proof of MIPT Phase Transition

Proposition 2.

Consider the MIPT recurrence ht=(1−p)​ei​θ​ht−1+p​bth_{t}=(1-p)e^{i\theta}h_{t-1}+pb_{t} with constant pp and i.i.d. inputs. The approximate entanglement entropy satisfies:

  • •

    p→0p\to 0: S~t→log⁡D\tilde{S}_{t}\to\log D (wave phase, maximum entropy)

  • •

    p→1p\to 1: S~t→\tilde{S}_{t}\to input entropy (particle phase)

The critical point is N∗=D/p​e​f​fN^{*}=D/p_{\emph{eff}} where p​e​f​f=𝔼⁡[p¯t]p_{\emph{eff}}=\mathbb{E}[\bar{p}_{t}].

Proof sketch.

Wave limit: TT uncorrelated phase rotations yield near-uniform amplitude distribution, maximizing S~\tilde{S}. Particle limit: hT≈bTh_{T}\approx b_{T}, so entropy equals input entropy. Crossover when the effective memory horizon τ=−1/log(1−peff)≈1/peff\tau=-1/\log(1-p_{\text{eff}})\approx 1/p_{\text{eff}} satisfies τ≈D\tau\approx D. ∎

Remark. If peffp_{\text{eff}} is approximately constant across task scales, then N∗=D⋅ξN^{*}=D\cdot\xi where ξ=1/peff\xi=1/p_{\text{eff}} is the task-specific coherence constant.

Gradient flows through the attention output: tokens that improve retrieval when cached receive positive gradient on ptp_{t}.
